rows.narrative: On September [XXX], 2026 at 1:27 AM PDT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on [XXX] at [XXX]. The Waymo AV was traveling southwestbound in the rightmost lane on [XXX] and proceeding straight at a green light through the intersection with [XXX]. As the Waymo AV entered the intersection, a passenger car traveling northwestbound on [XXX] entered the intersection against a red light at [XXX] at a high rate of speed, approaching the Waymo AV from the left. The Waymo AV slowed to yield to the passenger car as the passenger car continued forward and entered the Waymo AV's lane of travel, and the right side of the passenger car made contact with the front of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage. The passenger in the Waymo AV alleged minor injuries. Waymo became aware of the tow on September 9, 2026 after an additional review of available information. Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because a vehicle involved was towed away. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

The Zoox vehicle slowed to a gradual stop and then started to move forward, waiting for a gap in traffic to change lanes to the right, when Vehicle 2 driver passed it on the left side, striking the left rear fender. The Vehicle 2 driver did not stop at the scene to exchange information. The Zoox vehicle resumed operation and returned to base for inspection. The Zoox vehicle was found to have sustained minor damage. There were no reported injuries, and police were not notified.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in autonomous mode and traveling northwest on 17th Street toward Idaho Avenue in Santa Monica slowed to a gradual stop with its brake and hazard lights activated during a simulated pick-up/drop-off maneuver when the right side mirror of a cargo van (Vehicle 2), passing on the left, swiped the left side mirror of the stopped Zoox vehicle. There were no reported injuries, and police were not notified.

On February 2, 2026 at 12:46 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a bus on Portola Drive near Teresita Boulevard. The Waymo AV was stopped facing northeast on Portola Drive in the fourth from the right lane in a queue of traffic for a red light at the intersection with O’Shaughnessy Boulevard. While the Waymo AV was stopped, a bus traveling northbound on Teresita Boulevard turned right onto Portola Drive behind the Waymo AV, and began to enter the beginning of the dedicated left turn lane adjacent to the Waymo AV. The Waymo AV began to move a short distance to create additional room for the bus to complete its right turn before coming to a stop. While the Waymo AV was stopped, the bus continued to complete the right turn and the right side of the bus made contact with the rear left side of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

An unoccupied Zoox autonomous vehicle was traveling in the right lane on northwest-bound 9th Street, slowing and preparing to make a right turn onto Mission Street with a green traffic light. Partway through the right turn, the Zoox vehicle further slowed to yield to a pedestrian crossing Mission St, and at that time, a cyclist traveling northwest on the adjacent sidewalk rapidly entered the crosswalk. The Zoox vehicle braked to yield to the approaching cyclist, and the cyclist made contact with the right rear side of the nearly stopped Zoox vehicle. The bicycle fell to the ground, but its rider remained upright. The cyclist picked up their bicycle and rode away from the scene. Shortly after, the Zoox vehicle resumed operation to return to base. There was minor damage to the Zoox vehicle. There were no reported injuries, and police were not notified.

rows.location: Mitten Road near Old Bayshore Highway
rows.narrative: On February 1, 2026 at 5:12 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Burlingame, California made contact with the pavement in a parking lot driveway entrance on Mitten Road near Old Bayshore Highway. The Waymo AV was traveling southwestbound on Mitten Road and began to turn left at the parking lot driveway entrance at 1799 Old Bayshore Highway when the underside of the Waymo AV made contact with the pavement. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present in the driver’s seating position. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

An occupied Zoox autonomous vehicle (Vehicle 1) was traveling east on 24th Street toward Capp Street in San Francisco when a passenger vehicle (Vehicle 2) pulled out of the parking lane in an apparent attempt to merge into traffic. The Zoox vehicle slowed and biased away from Vehicle 2, but the left front corner of Vehicle 2 made contact with the right rear wheel of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage to the right rear wheel. The police were notified and arrived at the scene. One of the passengers in the Zoox vehicle initially noted their "neck hurts", but later stated they were "good" and declined medical attention.

rows.narrative: An occupied Zoox autonomous vehicle began to proceed on a fresh green traffic signal on westbound 15th Street at Mission Street when the driver of a stationary passenger vehicle (Vehicle 2), parallel-parked in the curb lane, rapidly opened the driver door into the path of the approaching Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle braked hard and attempted to steer left, but contact was unavoidable. The right side front fender, wheels, bodyside, and door panels made contact with the outside edge of the opening door of Vehicle 2. The Zoox vehicle came to an immediate stop and was later towed from the scene to be inspected for damage. First responders arrived at the scene. The passenger of the Zoox vehicle did not report any injuries. Later media stories reported the driver of Vehicle 2 had a “smashed hand” and his “hand was hurting, and that he was also experiencing pain to his neck area and lower back” based on a third party’s account, and that the driver “declined their offer to take him to the hospital.” Zoox vehicle camera footage shows clearly that no part of the robotaxi came into contact with the driver themselves, and that their hands, leg, and body did not interact with either the robotaxi or the parked vehicle’s door at any moment during the contact event.

The Waymo AV was traveling eastbound on Rolland Curtis Place in autonomous mode and came to a stop to stage a maneuver towards the curb and to yield to a passenger car traveling westbound on Rolland Curtis Place. After the passenger car passed the Waymo AV, the Waymo AV proceeded forward, came to a stop, and then reversed into a vacant space at the curb in between two parked passenger cars. The Waymo AV came to a stop at the curb. The test driver of the Waymo AV then transitioned to manual mode and reversed, and the rear of the Waymo AV made contact with the front of the passenger car that was parked behind the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in autonomous mode was eastbound on 17th Street, preparing to make an unprotected left turn onto Valencia Street in San Francisco. As the Zoox vehicle slowed approaching the intersection at Valencia Street, a left-turning vehicle in the oncoming lane accelerated abruptly. The Zoox vehicle braked in response to the oncoming vehicle, and was rear ended by a passenger car (Vehicle 2) traveling directly behind. The Zoox vehicle operator then disengaged from autonomy, and shortly after, continued through the intersection along 17th Street and pulled over to exchange information. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage to the rear end, and Vehicle 2 appears to have sustained moderate damage to the left front area and hood. The Zoox vehicle operator and the software operator, seated in the front passenger seat, reported injuries after the collision. The police were not called.

rows.narrative: On October 12, 2025 at 12:07 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Redwood City, California was in a collision involving a curb and later a speed bump in a parking lot at 1455 Madison Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling northeastbound on Vera Avenue in the parking lot at 1455 Madison Avenue when it initiated a U-turn over a curb partitioning parking stalls. While proceeding over the dividing curb, the undercarriage of the Waymo AV made contact with the curb and the left side rail trim of the Waymo AV partially detached. After the Waymo AV completed the U-turn, the Waymo AV traveled southwestbound on Vera Avenue, turned right onto northwestbound Saint Francis Street, and parked for a passenger pick-up. After remaining stopped for approximately five minutes, the passenger pick-up was cancelled and the Waymo AV traveled northwestbound on Saint Francis Street for a short distance and then proceeded over a rubber speed bump. As the Waymo AV traveled over the rubber speed bump, the partially detached left side rail trim of the Waymo AV caught on the rubber speed bump. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV and the speed bump sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in autonomous mode was stopped at a stop sign on southbound Bryant Street at 18th Street in San Francisco. The Zoox vehicle camera footage shows that the driver of Vehicle 2 was not looking ahead at the roadway before or at the time of contact. The police were not called.

An unoccupied Zoox autonomous vehicle (Vehicle 1) was traveling northeast on a green traffic light on Brannan Street at 8th Street in San Francisco. rows.narrative: The Ohmio Lift was driving on Gemende Drive towards Airport Drive in Riverside California. A minivan reversed out of a parking position (perpendicular parking to road lane) from the right side of the road into the shuttle’s path and struck the shuttle from the side. Summary of Events -Upon detecting the minivan in the side envelope, the system issued a brake command within 5ms. -Brake pressure began rising 58ms after the command and exceeded 90% of the requested pressure 164ms after the initial command. -The minivan reversed out of a parking space perpendicular to the Ohmio Lift’s direction of travel and struck the Lift on the side. -The minivan continued reversing until contact occurred. -The elapsed time from first detection of the minivan in the side envelope to impact was approximately 358ms. -The vehicle came to a complete stop in 1.178 seconds.

rows.location: 15th Street between Wiese Street and Mission Street
rows.narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) was operating in autonomous mode, traveling east in the right lane of 15th Street between Mission and Wiese Streets in San Francisco. As it approached a double-parked passenger car (Vehicle 2) in the lane, the operator of the Zoox vehicle disengaged from autonomous driving. The operator then moved into the left lane and maneuvered around Vehicle 2. The driver of Vehicle 2 started moving just as the Zoox vehicle was re-entering the right lane, and shortly after, the right front area of the Zoox vehicle made contact with the left front area of Vehicle 2. The Zoox vehicle did not sustain any damage, but Vehicle 2 sustained moderate damage to its left front door. There were no reported injuries, and the police were not called.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in autonomous mode turned right onto Laguna Street from eastbound Hermann Street, approaching the intersection with Market Street in San Francisco. As it was entering the intersection, the Zoox vehicle briefly braked to a stop, and just as it started to move, it was rear ended by a passenger car (Vehicle 2) traveling directly behind. The Zoox vehicle operator then disengaged from autonomy, cleared the intersection, and pulled over to exchange information. The rear bumper of the Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage, and its software operator, who was seated in the front passenger seat, reported "soreness in [the] right shoulder" after the collision. The police were not called

On May 14, 2025 at 6:54 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Venice Boulevard near Frances Avenue. The Waymo AV was in autonomous mode traveling northeast on Venice Boulevard in the right lane. As the Waymo AV reached the intersection with Frances Avenue, a dog entered the roadway from the southeast sidewalk. The Waymo AV began braking and then the test driver assumed manual control of the Waymo AV and continued braking. As the Waymo AV came to a stop, the dog continued to cross in front of the Waymo AV. A passenger car traveling behind the Waymo AV swerved to the left, and the front passenger side of the passenger car made contact with the rear driver side of the Waymo AV. Following the initial contact, the passenger car continued into the lane to the left of the Waymo AV, struck the dog, and then came to a stop in the left lane. The dog then left the scene. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in autonomous mode and traveling northeast on Bryant Street, was preparing to make a right on red traffic light on 10th Street in San Francisco. After fully stopping at the stop line, it advanced into the crosswalk before yielding to cross traffic with the right of way. A bicyclist, riding northwest on the sidewalk along 10th Street, then approached the crosswalk. As the bicyclist entered the crosswalk, the operator of the Zoox vehicle disengaged from autonomy and began to manually drive the vehicle forward. The bicyclist veered right towards the front of the Zoox vehicle and made contact with the front passenger side door of the Zoox vehicle. The bicycle then fell to the ground next to the Zoox vehicle. After stopping for a brief conversation with the bicyclist, the Zoox vehicle operator proceeded to make the right turn onto 10th Street, inadvertently driving over the front wheel of the fallen bicycle. The operator completed the turn and pulled over to check for damages and exchange information. The Zoox vehicle did not sustain any damage; however, the front wheel rim of the bicycle was damaged. There were no reported injuries, and the police were not notified.

rows.av_damage_areas: left rear; left rear passenger; front driver side; left front corner
rows.narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in autonomous mode, was heading east on Alameda Street toward Harrison Street in San Francisco. It then encountered a van hauling a trailer (Vehicle 2) traveling west, partially occupying both the westbound and eastbound lanes on Alameda Street. The Zoox vehicle slowed for the oncoming Vehicle 2; then its operator disengaged from autonomy and manually brought the vehicle to a complete stop. As Vehicle 2 passed, the driver's side of Vehicle 2 scraped the driver's side of the stopped Zoox vehicle. The driver of Vehicle 2 failed to stop and exchange information. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage, and no injuries were reported. Camera footage from the Zoox vehicle shows that the operator of Vehicle 2 steered toward it without appearing to attempt to avoid making contact. The police were later notified about the incident.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in autonomous mode was stopped for a red traffic light on north-westbound 9th Street, waiting to turn left onto Howard Street in San Francisco. After the light turned green, and before the Zoox vehicle started to move, it was rear ended by a passenger car (Vehicle 2) that was traveling directly behind. The Zoox vehicle operator then disengaged from autonomy, completed the left turn, and pulled over on Howard Street to exchange information. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage to the rear bumper. There were no reported injuries, and police were not called. The Zoox vehicle camera footage shows that the Vehicle 2 driver was not looking ahead at the roadway before or at the time of contact.

rows.location: On Bryant St at Division St
rows.narrative: An unoccupied Zoox vehicle in autonomous mode was traveling south on Bryant Street, slowing and preparing to make a right turn onto Division Street in San Francisco. At that time, an approaching e-scooterist was also traveling south on Bryant Street in the curb lane offset from the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle braked to a stop as the e-scooterist was beginning to enter the intersection. The e-scooterist then made contact with the right rear side of the stopped Zoox vehicle, and the e-scooterist fell to the ground next to the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle then started to move and completed the right turn onto Treat Avenue, coming to a stop a short distance down Treat Avenue. The e-scooterist then walked themself and the e-scooter over to the sidewalk, where they were met by a member of the Zoox operations team, and they reported “[a] chipped tooth and jaw pain.” The e-scooterist declined medical attention and rode their e-scooter from the scene after exchanging information. There was no damage to the Zoox vehicle and the police were not called.

A Zoox vehicle operating in manual mode was parallel-parked on eastbound Bay Street in San Francisco when an SUV (Vehicle 2), traveling east in the adjacent lane, swiped the driver's side mirror on the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage. The operator of Vehicle 2 did not stop and left the scene without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries, and police were not called.

rows.location: On First lane from right near 2772 San Tomas Expy
rows.av_damage_areas: front driver side; left front corner
rows.narrative: At 2:23pm: WeRide driverless vehicle (vehicle 1) was travelling ~45mph without much traffic ahead when a BMW x3 (vehicle 2) travelling in the adjacent left lane and in the same direction, merged into vehicle 1's left front quarter panel. Vehicle 1 and Vehicle 2 sustained moderate damages. After discussing the incident with vehicle 2's driver, they admitted they were attempting to make an upcoming right turn off the expressway. They initiated 2 consecutive right lane changes abruptly before hitting vehicle 1 on their last attempted lane change. After the initial impact, vehicle 1 was forced out of the initial lane, onto a divide, and ultimately came to a stop on the shoulder of the expressway. At this time both occupants of vehicle 1 and vehicle 2 were able to assess respective damages and exchange information. It was determined that there were no injuries. Vehicle 1 required a tow back to the facility.

rows.narrative: On May 1, 2025 at 7:52 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Portola Valley, California was in a collision involving a pickup truck tire on Junipero Serra Freeway near Exit 22. The Waymo AV was traveling northwestbound in the rightmost lane on Junipero Serra Freeway when the rear passenger side tire of a pickup truck traveling directly in front of the Waymo AV became dislodged and rolled into the barrier on the right edge of the roadway, then bounced off the barrier and into the Waymo AV's lane of travel. The Waymo AV activated its left turn signal and began to change lanes into the adjacent lane to the left and the test driver assumed manual control of the AV to move more aggressively to the left. As the AV was moving to the left, the tire made contact with the passenger side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged in autonomous mode due to the test driver assuming manual control 0.8s before impact. A test driver was present in the driver’s seating position. The Waymo AV and the tire sustained damage.

rows.location: Parking lot near E. 8th Street and Damon Street
rows.narrative: On April 25, 2025 at 12:54 PM PT, a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, California was involved in a collision involving a passenger vehicle. The Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged until approximately two seconds before the collision. The Waymo AV was traveling southeast through a narrow stretch of a parking lot when it reached a closed gate. It reversed along the same path and then began a multi-point turn to continue traveling northwest through the parking lot. Midway through executing this multi-point turn and while the Waymo AV was stationary, the Waymo AV was disengaged and then reversed into a parked passenger vehicle while in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained minor damage.

rows.narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in autonomous mode, was gradually slowing to a stop for a red traffic signal on southbound Bryant Street at the intersection with 17th Street in San Francisco when it was rear-ended by a passenger car (Vehicle 2) traveling directly behind. The Zoox vehicle operator then disengaged from autonomy. Both vehicles proceeded a few feet further and pulled over to exchange information. Both the Zoox vehicle and Vehicle 2 sustained minor damage. The police were not called. The Zoox vehicle operator reported back pain after the collision.

rows.location: Intersection of 9th Street and Folsom Street
rows.narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) was operating in autonomous mode, traveling northwest in the right lane of 9th Street and preparing to turn right onto Folsom Street in San Francisco. As it approached the crosswalk on Folsom Street, the Zoox vehicle gradually slowed; its operator disengaged from autonomy and continued to slow to yield to a pedestrian with the right-of-way entering the crosswalk. At that time, a passenger car (Vehicle 2), traveling directly behind the Zoox vehicle, struck the left rear corner of the Zoox vehicle. The driver of Vehicle 2 did not stop and continued along 9th Street after the incident. The Zoox vehicle incurred moderate damage, and the police were not notified. The operator later reported experiencing a "back spasm."

While traveling northbound on[XXX] in Martinez, a car pulled out of a driveway on the right side without right of way and collided with the right side of May's vehicle (t-bone.) May's vehicle was traveling at approximately 20 MPH in a residential neighborhood, and was approximately 1m left of lane center when a black vehicle exited a driveway on the right from behind a fence, facing the road and May's vehicle. This vehicle did not slow down or stop until entering into the roadway and collided with the May vehicle's right side. AVO attempts to swerve to the left but is unable to avoid a collision. The primary factor that led to the collision was the other vehicles action proceeding without the right-of-way into the side of the May vehicle. Upon further inspection, it was determined that we did not predict this collision until it was too late to avoid it even by veering. The velocity of the other vehicle was underestimated and was largely given only yield policies as having the most significant likelihood. There is some room for improvement in our response, which we plan to implement in future software releases, namely, an emergency veer policy must exist that is capable of moving quickly and far enough to possibly avoid the collision, more accurate reporting of velocity for slow-moving agents, estimate acceleration when assessing risk, improvements to predictions of the probability of an agent yielding, and adjusting our risk assessment so that it is heading dependent and more risk would be associated with passing close in front of another vehicle.

On January [XXX], 2025 at 6:07 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (Waymo AV) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle near the intersection of [XXX] and [XXX]. While the Waymo AV and the other passenger vehicle were stopped, an SUV approached from behind at an extreme rate of speed and made contact with the passenger vehicle behind the Waymo AV, which then made contact with the rear bumper of the Waymo AV. According to the San Francisco Police Department, the Waymo AV then began to rotate clockwise and, as it was rotating, the front of the SUV made contact with the passenger side of the Waymo AV. The rear of the Waymo AV then made contact with the rear driver side corner of another passenger car that had just begun to proceed straight on northbound [XXX]. According to the San Francisco Police Department, at least two other vehicles were involved in the crash and one of the occupants of the vehicles involved in the crash and a domestic animal were declared deceased at the scene. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AVs Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV, the passenger vehicle behind the Waymo AV, and the SUV sustained severe damage. The extent of the damage to the other three vehicles is currently unknown. Waymo received notice that five passengers in four of the vehicles involved sustained injuries of varying severity. Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because of a fatality. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On December [XXX], 2024 at 8:28 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, CA was in a collision involving two SUV's, a passenger car, and a pick up truck on [XXX] at [XXX]. The Waymo AV was stopped in autonomous mode facing south at a red light as the lead vehicle in the second from the right lane when an SUV traveling northbound in an oncoming traffic lane ran the red light. As the oncoming SUV entered the intersection, it made contact with a passenger car traveling east on [XXX]. The oncoming SUV continued through the intersection and swerved to narrowly miss a pedestrian before making contact with the front of the Waymo AV and the front driver side of a stationary pickup truck to the right of the Waymo AV. The impact from the oncoming SUV caused the Waymo AV to contact another SUV that was also stationary to the left of the Wayo AV at the red traffic light. The Waymo AV test driver transitioned to manual mode immediately before the oncoming SUV made contact. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage to the front and rear of the vehicle, necessitating a tow from the scene. The oncoming SUV sustained damage to the front and driver side. The stationary SUV that was contacted sustained damage to the passenger side. The Waymo test driver was transported to a local hospital for medical treatment. Transdev Alternative Services is reporting this crash under Request no. 1 of Standing General order 2021-01 because an individual involved was transported from the scene to a hospital for medical treatment, a vehicle involved was towed away, and because of airbag deployment. Transdev may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available. This is a duplicate of NHTSA Report ID: 30270-9476-2.

rows.location: In Intersection Coleman Ave Left turn to W Hedding St
rows.narrative: On November 27th at 1:27pm, Car 1 (weride av) - while in autonomous mode - was making a legal, protected, left turn from Coleman Ave. Car 1, turning onto W Hedding St., performed the turn from the second lane from the left and was travelling 11 mph when Car 1 then slowed down while still in the intersection. It is at this time Car 1's safety driver disengaged Car 1 from autonomous mode by using the throttle; this put car 1 into manual mode. It is at this time when car 2 (Ford f-150 XLT), traveling at 18 mph and also making a left turn from Coleman Ave within the same lane as car 1, struck and rear ended car 1 while both cars were still in the intersection. Car 1 sustained minor damage to its rear bumper and car 2 sustained minor damage to front bumper. Both parties pulled over to exchange information. Car 2 did not provide Registration and Insurance for their respective car. Car 2's driver did give us driver's license information but the driver of the vehicle (car 2) at the time of the incident was a different person than that represented on the driver's license presented.

A Zoox vehicle in autonomous mode was stopped for a red traffic light on northbound Howard Street while preparing to turn left onto westbound 12th Street in San Francisco. After the light turned green the Zoox vehicle began to move forward and then slowed gradually to yield to a pedestrian with right of way in the crosswalk on 12th Street. Just as the Zoox vehicle slowed to almost a stop (0.2 mph), a skateboarder quickly approached the rear of the Zoox vehicle extending their left arm forward and making contact with the right rear corner of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle operator then disengaged from autonomy and brought the vehicle to a stop. The skateboarder initially told the Zoox vehicle operator they were not injured but later mentioned they “smacked” their hand and it was “bruised.” When asked, however, they declined medical attention. The Zoox vehicle did not sustain damage. The police were not called. The Zoox vehicle camera footage shows that the skateboarder was looking at their cell phone and did not appear to have been looking ahead at the roadway before the time of contact.

rows.narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in manual mode, was stopped for a red traffic light on northbound Van Ness Avenue, at the intersection with Mission St in San Francisco. A passenger car (Vehicle 2), traveling in the same direction, was stopped in the adjacent lane to the right of the Zoox vehicle. As the signal turned green, both vehicles proceeded forward and shortly after that Vehicle 2 suddenly veered left into Zoox vehicle's travel lane. The driver side quarter panel of Vehicle 2 made contact with the passenger side fender of the Zoox vehicle. The quarter panel of Vehicle 2 appeared to have scrapes and there was no damage to the Zoox vehicle. There were no reported injuries and police were not called.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), was completing a mission traveling southwest on Division Street in San Francisco. As the vehicle was completing its mission and slowed to a near stop, the Zoox vehicle operator identified an oncoming bicycle, disengaged from autonomy, and braked the Zoox vehicle to a full stop in its lane. The bicyclist crossed into the oncoming traffic lane occupied by the Zoox vehicle and continued rapidly while steering directly towards the front of the Zoox vehicle. The bicycle made contact with the front bumper of the stationary Zoox vehicle and the bicyclist made contact with the hood of the Zoox vehicle and fell to the ground. The police and emergency responders arrived at the scene and the bicyclist was transported to a hospital. Preliminary police information describes injuries to the bicyclist as “loss of consciousness, complaint of pain to back, knee, and toe nail”.

rows.location: On 16th Street at the intersection with Utah Street

The Zoox vehicle operator disengaged from autonomy and braked further for stopped traffic ahead in the same travel lane. At that time, a Tesla sedan (Vehicle 2) traveling directly behind the Zoox vehicle abruptly attempted a lane change maneuver into the adjacent lane on the right, side-swiping a BMW sedan (Vehicle 3) that was also westbound on 16th Street in the right lane. Vehicle 2, after making contact with Vehicle 3, veered back to the left lane behind the Zoox vehicle and rear ended the stopped Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage, while Vehicle 2 and Vehicle 3 appeared to have sustained moderate damage. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

rows.location: Chess Drive approaching Foster City Blvd
rows.narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was traveling westbound on Chess Drive in Foster City when a parallel-parked passenger car (Vehicle 2) abruptly entered the Zoox vehicle’s travel lane from a parking space in the right parking lane without yielding or activating a turn signal. Vehicle 2 made contact with the right front side and wheel of the Zoox vehicle, and the Zoox vehicle made contact with the driver's side door and left front tire/wheel well of the passenger car. Both vehicles sustained moderate damage and the Zoox vehicle was towed from the scene. There were no reported injuries at that time and police were not called. Zoox is submitting this updated report to include new information on an unspecified "soft tissue injury" claim received on December 3, 2024, from one of the passengers in Vehicle 2. This update provides complete information to date for this incident.

On Wednesday, May 22, 2024 at approximately 3:45pm PST, a Nuro Prius operating in manual mode bumped a pedestrian at the intersection of Webster Street and Middlefield Road in Palo Alto, California. The Nuro Prius was in autonomous mode when it approached the intersection and came to a stop at the stop bar on Webster Street. It is a two-way stop with the traffic on Middlefield having right of way. The Nuro Prius nudged forward due to an occlusion.The Nuro operator judged the nudging to be too far and disengaged autonomous mode to reverse in manual. When reversing, the operator bumped a pedestrian crossing the street behind the Nuro Prius. The pedestrian was not injured and after speaking with the operator, left the scene without providing additional information. There was no damage to the vehicle and law enforcement was not involved.

rows.narrative: On May 20, 2024 at 3:02 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on 14th Street at Folsom Street. The Waymo AV was traveling east on 14th Street and came to a stop at a red light at the intersection with Folsom Street to prepare for a left turn. When the light turned green, the Waymo AV proceeded into the intersection. As it did so, a passenger car traveling southbound on Folsom Street at a high rate of speed entered the intersection against a red traffic light. The front of the passenger car made contact with the driver’s side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage, and the passengers of the passenger car left the scene on foot.

On May 17, 2024 at 11:45 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Interstate 280 North between exits 54B and 55. The Waymo AV was traveling north on Interstate 280 in the rightmost lane in autonomous mode with a test driver seated in the driver's seated position when it approached a slow-moving heavy truck equipped with a truck-mounted light matrix displaying a yellow arrow indicating that traffic should merge to the left. The Waymo AV slowed down behind the heavy truck and the test driver transitioned the Waymo AV to manual mode. The test driver stopped the Waymo AV and activated the left turn signal. Several vehicles passed the Waymo AV on the left side before the test driver manually initiated a left lane change, and the front passenger side of a passenger car which was passing the Waymo AV on the left made contact with the front driver side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

rows.narrative: On May 15, 2024, the front right bumper of a Pony.ai autonomous vehicle (AV) scraped against a flexible plastic traffic pylon on Auto Mall Pkwy near the intersection of Auto Mall Pkwy & Grimmer Blvd, in Fremont, CA. The vehicle was operating in supervised autonomous (“Drivered”) mode. There were no other vehicles, pedestrians, or road users involved. Following the incident, the safety operator pulled over in a safe location and confirmed there was only minor cosmetic damage to the front bumper of the AV. The safety operator then promptly drove the vehicle, in manual mode, to Pony.ai’s Fremont office. There were no injuries, and the police were not called.

The passenger car then made contact with the center median and came to a stop. The Waymo AV was transitioned into manual mode, and the test driver stopped the Waymo AV to the right-hand shoulder. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

A Ghost ADS-equipped car was driving engaged Northbound on Highway 17. As always, there were two safety drivers in the car. Traffic was moving in all four lanes at or near the speed limit. The Ghost vehicle was in the right-middle lane. Another vehicle (the "lead" car) entered into the Ghost car's lane from the right. While there were numerous vehicles ahead of the Ghost car before that vehicle entered the lane, the lead vehicle blocked the view of the lane before it. Throughout the incident, traffic in the other three lanes continued at a steady pace. When the lead vehicle entered into the lane ahead of the Ghost car, the Ghost car applied the brakes to accommodate the intrusion and then continued to match the speed of the lead car. The lead car suddenly slammed the brakes. The Ghost car followed suit, reducing its speed from 19 mps (42.5 mph) to 4.7 mps (10.5 mph) within the next three seconds. The Ghost car was able to match the rapid speed reduction of the lead car and avoid contact. The driver following the Ghost car was not able to respond as quickly as the Ghost ADS. When the following driver began to apply the brakes, the car was about five meters behind and was traveling at 6.5 mps. At the point of impact, the Ghost vehicle was traveling at 4.78 mps (10.7 mph), matching the lead car. There were no injuries. The vehicles suffered only cosmetic damage, the drivers exchanged information, and the Ghost safety drivers returned to home base in conventional mode.

Transdev may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available. This is a duplicate of report ID 30270-6351-1.

On September [XXX], 2023 at 6:26 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (Waymo AV) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on [XXX] at [XXX]. While the Waymo AV was stopped in park waiting to pick up a passenger near the right side curb of the road on westbound [XXX], a passenger car that was passing the stopped Waymo AV made contact with the rear drivers side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AVs Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage. Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because a vehicle involved was towed away. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On August 24, 2023 at 4:39 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Santa Monica, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Michigan Avenue at Euclid Street. The Waymo AV was traversing a roundabout at the intersection of Michigan Avenue at Euclid Street when it slowed to a stop for other vehicles approaching and in the roundabout. The front of the passenger car that was in the roundabout behind the Waymo AV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. Both vehicles sustained damage.

rows.location: 9th St at Seven Seas Ave, Treasure Island
rows.narrative: At approximately 5:54 p.m. PST on Wednesday, August 23, 2023, at the intersection of Seven Seas Ave and 9th Street on Treasure Island in the city of San Francisco, a Beep-operated autonomous shuttle was proceeding in autonomous mode straight E/B after stopping at a 3-way stop intersection when a vehicle making a left turn heading N/B proceeded out of turn resulting in a collision within the intersection. There were no passengers on board and no injuries reported. Both vehicle sustained minor damage and police did not respond to the scene. There were no other witness statements received.

On August 23, 2023 at 9:54 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck on Mason Street at Vandewater Street. The Waymo AV was traveling northbound on Mason Street when it approached a heavy truck and trailer that was stopped in the adjacent lane on the left side of the street. As the Waymo began to slowly pass the truck, the truck initiated a reversing turn maneuver into a loading bay on the left side of Mason Street. The Waymo AV then came to a stop, and as the Waymo AV was initiating its own reversing maneuver to clear the path for the truck, the right side of the trailer made contact with the front driver’s side corner of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

rows.location: Martin Luther King Jr. Drive at Crossover Drive
rows.narrative: On August 20, 2023 at 5:49 PM PT the mirror of a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was struck by a cyclist on Martin Luther King Jr. Drive at Crossover Drive. The Waymo AV was stopped in traffic on eastbound Martin Luther King Jr. Drive at the intersection with Crossover Drive, when a cyclist that had been traveling behind the Waymo AV passed the Waymo AV on the left. As the cyclist passed the Waymo AV, the cyclist made contact with the driver side mirror of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained damage and the cyclist did not stop, leaving the scene without exchanging information.

rows.av_damage_areas: left rear; rear bumper; right rear
rows.narrative: On August 19, 2023 at 4:45 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on 13th Street at Mission Street. The Waymo AV entered the slip lane which connects westbound 13th Street to northbound Mission Street and came to a stop to yield to cross-traffic on Mission Street. As the Waymo AV was stopped, the front of the passenger car which was traveling behind the Waymo AV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained damage.

rows.av_damage_areas: left rear; rear bumper; right rear; left rear passenger; front driver side
rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“AV”), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on eastbound 26th Street at the intersection with Mission Street. As the AV was proceeding after the light turned green, a Dodge Charger traveling southbound on Mission Street failed to stop for the red light, entered the intersection, and made contact with the AV, damaging the front and rear driver side and rear bumper fascia of the AV. Police and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) were called to the scene. The AV was towed from the scene. The passenger of the Dodge Charger was assessed by medical personnel at the scene and was not transported by EMS.

rows.manufacturer: Mercedes-Benz Research & Development North America, Inc.
rows.av_damage_areas: left rear; rear bumper; right rear
rows.narrative: The driver was manually driving the Mercedes-Benz vehicle on the interchange from the 105W to 405S when the vehicle in front of him came to an abrupt stop due to slowed traffic on the freeway. The driver manually brought the Mercedes-Benz vehicle to a stop in his lane. The vehicle behind him did not come to a stop in time and rear ended the Mercedes-Benz. There was no injury or property damage. The Mercedes-Benz was able to drive away from the accident. Damange was sustained to the rear bumper of the Mercedes Benz and the front bumper of the following vehicle. At no point during the incident was the vehicle operating in autonomous mode.

rows.av_damage_areas: left rear; left rear passenger; front driver side
rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a stop sign on eastbound 17th Street at the intersection with Vermont Street. As the AV began to proceed straight, a gray Honda Odyssey traveling westbound on 17th Street on the opposite side of the intersection from the AV entered the intersection and veered into the AV’s lane of travel. The AV stopped in response as the Honda Odyssey continued traveling in the AV’s lane of travel through the intersection and, shortly thereafter, the Honda Odyssey made contact with the AV, damaging the front and rear driver side doors, front driver side radar assembly and rear driver side tire of the AV. The parties exchanged information. There were no reported injuries and the AV was towed from the scene.

On August 17, 2023 at 1:05 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Bayshore Boulevard near Jerrold Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling northbound on Bayshore Boulevard. As the SUV was passing the Waymo AV to the left, it initiated a right lane change. The front of the SUV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage, and the SUV left the scene without exchanging information.

rows.manufacturer: Zoox, Inc. dba Zoox Labs Inc.
rows.narrative: A Zoox vehicle in manual mode was slowing (with brake lights illuminated) in bumper-to-bumper traffic on westbound Sagamore St. approaching Orizaba St. when it was struck from behind by a following vehicle (vehicle 2). There was minor damage apparent to the hood of the striking vehicle and no damage to the Zoox vehicle. There were no injuries and police were not called.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“AV”), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling southbound on Albion Street between 16th Street and Camp Street. At the same time, a Ford pickup truck was traveling northbound on Albion Street partially in the AV’s lane of travel. The AV stopped due to limited space to proceed forward due to the encroaching Ford pickup truck, and, shortly thereafter, the Ford pickup truck made contact with the AV, damaging the AV’s rear driver side bumper fascia, rear driver side quarter panel and rear driver side wheel molding. The driver of the Ford pickup truck left the scene without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries.

A registered Ghost AV Test vehicle was hit by crash debris while traveling on I-680 N. The Ghost vehicle neither hit nor was hit by another vehicle. The Ghost car was traveling in AV mode with a registered AV Test Driver behind the wheel and an additional Safety Co-Driver in the passenger seat. Traffic slowed quickly due to a crash ahead of the Ghost car. Consistent with their training, the Ghost driver took control by braking and disengaging the autonomous system. The Ghost car stopped without impacting the preceding car. A Mercedes car immediately following the Ghost car also came to a stop without impacting the Ghost car. Ghost's understanding based on communications at the scene is that a Grand Cherokee traveling behind the Mercedes tried to swerve to avoid impacting the Mercedes but clipped the Mercedes and rolled over. To Ghost's knowledge, nobody in the Grand Cherokee was injured. The Ghost drivers heard a noise and then found that the rear bumper of the Ghost car had been damaged, which Ghost believes resulted from crash debris. The Ghost drivers drove the Ghost car back to the garage in conventional mode.

On August 13, 2023 at 9:01 PM a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Howard Street at Fourth Street. The Waymo AV was traveling southwestbound on Howard Street in the second lane from the left as it was approaching Fourth Street. As the Waymo AV was proceeding straight through the intersection, the passenger car in the right adjacent lane made a left turn from a straight-only lane onto southeastbound Fourth Street. The rear of the passenger car made contact with the front of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both the Waymo AV and the passenger car sustained damage.

rows.location: North Curson Avenue at Waring Avenue
rows.narrative: On August 11, 2023 at 7:38 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a stationary object on North Curson Avenue at Waring Avenue. The Waymo AV was pulling over to the right side of the road, when the test driver transitioned to manual mode and made contact with a recycling bin on the right side of the street. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

rows.location: Van Ness Ave between Eddy St and Turk St
rows.narrative: At 1:45pm, a WeRide vehicle (Car 1) was parked at a Van Ness St. parking meter - between Eddy st. and Turk St. when another vehicle (Car 2) began reversing in front of the vehicle in question. The reversing vehicle (Car 2) ultimately collided with the front left corner of the WeRide vehicle (Car 1), causing minor damage to the front bumper. The reversing vehicle (Car 2) did not have any damage. Both drivers were able to confer with one another seconds after the incident took place. The reversing vehicle's driver did not possess any form of insurance or registration.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“AV”), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling northbound on Pennsylvania Avenue between 23rd Street and 25th Street when the AV approached a double-parked semi-trailer truck in the AV’s lane of travel. The AV began to maneuver around and to the left of the semi-trailer truck and came to a stop for a stop sign at the intersection with 23rd Street. At the same time, the semi-trailer truck proceeded forward and, shortly thereafter, made contact with the AV. This caused damage to the front passenger side bumper fascia of the AV. The parties exchanged information and there were no reported injuries.

On August 2, 2023 at 10:09 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Bush Street at Polk Street. The Waymo AV was stopped at a red light on eastbound Bush Street at Polk Street. Shortly after the traffic light turned green and the Waymo AV began to proceed forward, the Waymo AV slowed to a stop. The SUV that was traveling closely behind the Waymo AV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage, and the trailing SUV left the scene without exchanging information. A passenger in the Waymo AV reported injuries.

A Ghost autonomous vehicle was hit by crash debris while traveling on [XXX]. The Ghost vehicle neither hit nor was hit by another vehicle. The Ghost car was traveling in AV mode with two safety drivers. Traffic slowed quickly, apparently due to a crash ahead of the Ghost car. Consistent with their training, the Ghost driver took control of the car by manually braking and disengaging the autonomous system. The car was traveling 55.3 mph when the driver began to brake. The Ghost car stopped without impacting the preceding car. A Mercedes car immediately following the Ghost car also came to a stop without impacting the Ghost car. Ghost's understanding based on communications at the scene is that a Grand Cherokee traveling behind the Mercedes tried to swerve to avoid impacting the Mercedes but clipped the Mercedes and rolled over. To Ghost's knowledge, nobody in the Grand Cherokee was injured. The Ghost drivers heard a noise and then found that the rear bumper of the Ghost car had been damaged, which Ghost believes resulted from crash debris. The Ghost drivers drove the Ghost car back to the garage in conventional mode.

On July 29, 2023 at 2:57 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Santa Monica, California was in a collision involving a cyclist on Colorado Avenue near Ocean Avenue. The Waymo AV was stopped in traffic on southwestbound Colorado Avenue when a cyclist that had been traveling behind the Waymo AV passed the Waymo AV on the right. As the cyclist passed the Waymo AV, the cyclist made contact with the front passenger side sensor of the Waymo AV. rows.location: Leavenworth Street at Golden Gate Avenue
rows.narrative: On July 21, 2023 at 9:51 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Leavenworth Street at Golden Gate Avenue. The collision occurred while the Waymo AV was stopped in the leftmost lane of a two-lane, one-way road at the intersection of Leavenworth Street at Golden Gate Avenue. The Waymo AV was stopped before the intersection, yielding to blocking cross-traffic when the light turned yellow. At that point, a passenger car that had been stopped behind the Waymo AV passed the Waymo AV on the left and proceeded into the intersection. While passing the Waymo AV, the passenger car’s rear passenger side door made contact with the driver side rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The passenger car did not stop but appears to have sustained damage.

On July 11, 2023 at 10:13 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle on Martin Avenue at Mullen Avenue. While completing a right turn from Martin Avenue onto Mullen Avenue in autonomous mode, the Waymo AV slowed to a stop while entering a narrow roadway. As the Waymo AV started to slowly proceed forward, the test driver transitioned the vehicle to manual mode and proceeded forward, making contact with a parked passenger vehicle. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On July 8, 2023 at 3:08 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a cyclist on S. Alameda Street at 6th Street. As the Waymo AV was yielding to cross-traffic and preparing to make a right turn, a cyclist was traveling eastbound on 6th Street and heading the wrong way in the bike lane. The cyclist then turned left, northbound, onto S. Alameda Street, continuing to travel the wrong direction in the bike lane. As the Waymo AV slowly proceeded forward, the cyclist passed the Waymo AV and made contact with the rear passenger side sensor of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained damage and the cyclist did not stop, leaving the scene without exchanging information.

At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both the Waymo AV and the passenger car sustained damage.

On June 29, 2023 at 3:39 PM PDT, an Apollo Autonomous Vehicle (“Apollo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California, was in a collision involving a scooter on Moraga Street near 34th Ave. The Apollo AV was traveling westbound on Moraga Street passing the intersection with 34th Ave. The intersection has stop signs clearly installed at all four ways, which require vehicles to make full stop before entering the intersection. The Apollo AV made a full stop, entered and passed approximately 75% of the intersection. A person on scooter coming southbound from 34th Ave., approached the intersection. The person on scooter entered the intersection without stopping, then made contact with the passenger rear-side of Apollo AV. Our Apollo AV operator immediately disengaged the AV, pulled over to the closest safe place to park, got out of the car to check the person on scooter, who already left the scene on his scooter without exchanging any information. The Apollo AV had small minor paint scratch, which do not need repair. The police were not called.

As the semi-trailer truck began encroaching into the Cruise AV’s lane of travel, the Cruise AV operator disengaged from autonomous into manual mode and began reversing the Cruise AV, causing the Cruise AV to back into a different semi-trailer truck parked behind the Cruise AV. This caused damage to the Cruise AV’s rear passenger side wheel molding. The Cruise AV operator left information for the other party and there were no reported injuries.

The Fremont police took a report about the incident. There were no injuries reported.

On April 6, 2023 at 10:48 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck on Randall Street near Harper Street. The Waymo AV was proceeding northwest on Randall Street near the intersection with Harper Street when it came to a stop to yield to a heavy truck traveling southeast on Randall Street. As the heavy truck drove past the Waymo AV, the driver’s side section of the heavy truck made contact with the rear driver’s side sensor of the Waymo AV. The heavy truck then left the scene. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On April 5, 2023 at 10:46 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Potrero Avenue at 21st Street. The Waymo AV was traveling southbound on Potrero Avenue in the leftmost lane as it was approaching the intersection with 21st Street. The signal for traffic proceeding south on Potrero Avenue was green for the Waymo AV as it approached the intersection. As the Waymo AV approached, an individual riding a motorized scooter traveling north on Potrero Avenue proceeded to turn left onto westbound 21st Street, across the paths of the Waymo AV and other oncoming vehicles. The Waymo AV began to brake, and the Waymo AV test driver transitioned to manual mode and brought the Waymo AV to a stop. A passenger car traveling directly behind the Waymo AV then made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. The individual riding the scooter was not contacted by the Waymo AV or any other vehicle. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both the Waymo AV and the passenger car sustained damage, and the individual on the motorized scooter left the scene.

The SUV proceeded around the Waymo AV and made contact with the left rear sensor housing of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The driver of the SUV stopped briefly but left before sharing their information. The Waymo sustained damage.

rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling on westbound Haight Street between Ashbury Street and Masonic Avenue. At the same time, a San Francisco Municipal Railway (“MUNI”) Bus stopped ahead of the Cruise AV. Shortly thereafter, the Cruise AV made contact with the rear bumper of the MUNI Bus, damaging the front fascia and front fender of the Cruise AV. The parties exchanged information. There were no reported injuries and the Cruise AV was towed from the scene.

rows.av_damage_areas: left front corner; right front corner; front bumper
rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling southbound on Polk Street near the intersection with Clay Street. Shortly after passing through the intersection with Clay Street, the Cruise AV made contact with a downed power cable stretching across Polk Street and came to a stop. This caused damage to the Cruise AV’s front fascia. There were no injuries. Cruise was informed by law enforcement to keep the Cruise AV stationary until the power cables were cleared. During the time that the power cable was being cleared and that the Cruise AV was stopped, the Cruise AV ran low on battery power and did not have enough power to return to Cruise facilities on its own. The Cruise AV was therefore towed from the scene once the power cables were cleared.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“Cruise AV”), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling southbound on Shafter Avenue between Ingalls Street and Hawes Street. Shortly after the intersection with Ingalls Street, the Cruise AV made contact with a tow dolly attached to the back of a double-parked truck, damaging the front passenger side bumper and front passenger side fender of the Cruise AV. There were no reported injuries.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“Cruise AV”), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling westbound on Turk Boulevard between Roselyn Terrace and Kittredge Terrace. The Cruise AV came to a complete stop for a vehicle in the process of letting passengers out that was stopped in the Cruise AV’s lane of travel. A Smart Car traveling behind the Cruise AV came to a complete stop behind the Cruise AV. A Honda Accord trailing behind the Smart Car began to decelerate but made contact with the Smart Car, pushing the Smart Car forward into the Cruise AV’s rear bumper. The parties exchanged information. There were no damages to the Cruise AV and there were no reported injuries.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling eastbound on Clay Street between Hyde Street and Leavenworth Street. Shortly before the intersection with Leavenworth Street, the Cruise AV made contact with a downed power cable on Clay Street and came to a stop. This caused damage to the Cruise AV’s front driver side radar assembly. There were no injuries.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in manual mode, was traveling westbound in the leftmost lane on Sacramento Street between Larkin Street and Polk Street. As the Cruise AV operator attempted to parallel park behind a Hyundai Tucson, the Cruise AV made contact with the Hyundai Tucson. The parties exchanged information. There were no damages to the Cruise AV and there were no reported injuries.

On March 20, 2023 at 10:43 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Venice Boulevard at La Cienega. The Waymo AV was stopped in the center lane of a three-lane road behind a passenger vehicle for a red light facing southwest on Venice Boulevard at La Cienega in autonomous mode. The light turned green while cross-traffic remained backed up in the intersection. The Waymo AV nudged forward and slowed to a stop, yielding for the blocking cross traffic. A passenger vehicle that had been stopped behind the Waymo AV proceeded forward and made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On March 20, 2023 at approximately 8:04 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a pothole on Bayshore Boulevard near Jerrold Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling in the second lane on a four-lane section of northbound Bayshore Boulevard when the passenger side rear tire made contact with a pothole. The tire began to deflate and the Waymo AV pulled over on a side street. At the time of impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode.

rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on northbound Polk Street at the intersection with Sutter Street. The Cruise AV began to proceed as the light turned green when an Infiniti Q50 passed the Cruise AV in the oncoming traffic lane and began performing “donuts” in the intersection. The Cruise AV began to initiate a left turn onto Sutter Street when the Infiniti Q50 made contact with the Cruise AV’s front driver side bumper, causing damage to the front driver side bumper, front driver side fascia and front driver side headlight. The driver of the Infiniti Q50 left the scene without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries and the Cruise AV was towed from the incident.

The Cruise AV braked and the semi-trailer truck made contact with the left side of the Cruise AV, causing damage to the driver side front, rear, and bumper of the Cruise AV. The parties exchanged information and there were no injuries.

A Zoox vehicle in autonomy was proceeding straight on Harrison St. in San Francisco, Ca, when a passenger vehicle turning left from 14th St. on to Harrison St. struck the rear of the Zoox vehicle damaging the sensors. There were no injuries and the police were not called.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling southbound on 16th Avenue between Lomita Avenue and Lawton Street. Shortly thereafter, contact was made with the Cruise AV's front driver side mirror, damaging the front driver side mirror of the Cruise AV. The driver of the red Honda Sedan left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and a police report was later filed.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a stop sign on westbound Parnassus Avenue at the intersection with 4th Avenue. After the Cruise AV began to proceed straight through the intersection, a Toyota FJ Cruiser traveling southbound on 4th Avenue approached a stop sign in its direction of travel at the intersection with Parnassus Avenue. The Toyota FJ Cruiser did not stop for its stop sign and, shortly thereafter, the Toyota FJ Cruiser entered the intersection and made contact with the Cruise AV as the Cruise AV was passing through the intersection, damaging the rear passenger quarter panel of the Cruise AV. The driver of the Toyota FJ Cruiser left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and a police report was later filed.

rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling southbound in the right lane of traffic on Mission Street between Randall Street and Appleton Avenue. The Cruise AV stopped behind and to the left of a Hyundai Elantra that was stopped beside the right curb of Mission Street. The driver was standing beside the Hyundai Elantra with the driver door open into the lane of traffic. The Hyundai Elantra then rolled backwards at an angle and, shortly thereafter, made contact with the Cruise AV, damaging the front passenger door, rear passenger quarter panel, rear passenger bumper, and rear passenger wheel of the Cruise AV. The driver of the Hyundai Elantra left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and a police report was later filed.

At the time of impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained minor damage.

On July 2, 2022 at 6:54 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on the Embarcadero at Broadway. The signal for traffic proceeding north on the Embarcadero turned green, and traffic in adjacent lanes began moving. The left turn arrow signal for the dedicated turn lane occupied by the Waymo AV remained red. The passenger car that had been stopped directly behind the Waymo AV began moving forward. The front of the passenger car made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV, immediately after which the passenger car left the scene. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained minor damage and the Waymo AV test driver reported lower back pain.

The right rear corner of the passenger vehicle made contact with the front left corner of the Waymo AV, immediately after which the passenger car left the scene. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained minor damage.

rows.location: Parking Entrance near Brannan Street and 9th Street

The Waymo AV approached a parking lot. As the Waymo AV turned left and into the parking lot, the Waymo AV's undercarriage made contact with the driveway pavement (the AV did not contact any vehicle or road user). At the time of the contact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver's seating position). The Waymo AV sustained minor undercarriage damage.

rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“Cruise AV”), operating in manual mode, was stopped in a legal curbside parking spot on northbound Leavenworth Street between Francisco Street and Bay Street. A Mazda CX-9 approaching from the rear and traveling northbound on Leavenworth Street made contact with the Cruise AV’s rear driver side, damaging the left rear quarter panel of the Cruise AV resulting in the Cruise AV being towed from the incident. There is also damage to the Mazda CX-9’s right front quarter panel. There were no injuries reported and the police were not called.

rows.narrative: On June 14th, a test vehicle was operating in autonomous mode when the safety driver took manual control immediately before a white Mazda3 made contact with the rear of the test vehicle and caused damage to a sensor. This occurred as the test vehicle was making a right turn from Moorpark Way to East Evelyn Avenue in Mountain View. The test vehicle operators believed they had run over road debris and did not discover the crash or damage until after returning to base, so the two vehicles did not exchange information. No injuries were reported, and law enforcement was not called to the scene.

Norfolk St. and Eisenhower St. in San Mateo, CA, with a second vehicle stopped in the lane with its right turn indicator on, when a third vehicle overtook the second vehicle and cut in abruptly from the left, making contact with the front left side and sensors of the Zoox vehicle as it was exiting the space. The Zoox operator disengaged to manual mode just before the contact.

On June 5, 2022 at 10:07 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle on Bush Street and Gough Street. The Waymo AV was stopped in autonomous mode behind stopped traffic facing east on Bush Street. The passenger vehicle ahead of the Waymo AV transitioned into reverse and began to accelerate, making contact with the front sensor of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained minor damage.

rows.av_damage_areas: left rear; rear bumper; right rear; right rear passenger
rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV") operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling eastbound on Geary Boulevard toward the intersection with Spruce Street. As it approached the intersection, the Cruise AV entered the left hand turn lane, turned the left turn signal on, and initiated a left turn on a green light onto Spruce Street. At the same time, a Toyota Prius traveling westbound in the rightmost bus and turn lane of Geary Boulevard approached the intersection in the right turn lane. The Toyota Prius was traveling approximately 40 mph in a 25 mph speed zone. The Cruise AV came to a stop before fully completing its turn onto Spruce Street due to the oncoming Toyota Prius, and the Toyota Prius entered the intersection traveling straight from the turn lane instead of turning. Shortly thereafter, the Toyota Prius made contact with the rear passenger side of the Cruise AV. The impact caused damage to the right rear door, panel, and wheel of the Cruise AV. Police and Emergency Medical Services were called to the scene, and a police report was filed. The Cruise AV was towed from the scene. Occupants of both vehicles received medical treatment for allegedly minor injuries.

rows.av_damage_areas: left front corner; front bumper; right front corner
rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV") operating in supervised autonomous mode was driving Westbound on Hayes Street between Lyon Street and Baker Street when a pedestrian ran in front of the AV. rows.narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on southbound Masonic Avenue at the intersection with Oak Street. At the intersection, an Acura Sedan was stopped in front of the Cruise AV in the left southbound lane. To the right of the Cruise AV, was a BMW Sedan in the right southbound lane. In response to the green light, the Acura Sedan made a signaled left turn onto Oak Street as the BMW Sedan stayed parallel to the Cruise AV. As the Cruise AV entered the intersection, the BMW Sedan made a prohibited left turn from the right southbound lane on Masonic Avenue with no turn signal. The Cruise AV braked and, shortly thereafter, the BMW Sedan made contact with the Cruise AV, damaging the front right bumper of the Cruise AV. The driver of the BMW Sedan left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and Cruise filed a police report on February 12, 2022.

A moment later, a passenger vehicle turned right onto Silver Avenue from Mission Street into the oncoming traffic lane and swerved into the driver door of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained major damage. The test driver (in the driver’s seating position) transitioned to manual mode and continued to slow the Waymo AV. The motorcyclist attempted to turn behind the Waymo AV and made contact with the left rear corner of the Waymo AV. The motorcyclist remained upright and rode away without stopping to provide any information. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage to the driver’s side of the rear bumper.
